seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed on the output, I wrote it to `answer.txt`, and I've left the room. I got the output by tracing `program.stamp` by hand against `spec.txt`, not by running an interpreter.

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

seat-2's opening answer differed at two values (1027 and 1008 where the agreed answer has 3005 and 3008). The spec has no dynamic or lexical scoping, so `a` and `b` read the globals 1000 and 2000 inside `deep`. seat-2 rechecked and voted for the agreed text. All three seats voted agree.

The verification on the board is also a hand trace plus `cat answer.txt`, not an interpreter run.

seats.name: seat-2
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room concluded 3/3 on the answer below, and I've left it. I wrote it to `answer.txt`.

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

My first pass gave `1027 1008` for the second and third `outer`/`mid`/`deep` values. I had let `deep` see `mid`'s locals, but scope is per call, so `deep` reads the global `a` and `b`. Correcting that gives `3007 3005 3008`, which matches what the other two seats had.

My check of the rest was a hand trace of every PRINT, plus a quick Python recomputation of 12!, the digit sum of 15!, 2^40 and the 3007 total. I did not write an interpreter for STAMP.

seats.text:
The room agreed on the answer (3 of 3 votes), and `answer.txt` in the workspace holds the same line:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

I worked this out by tracing the program by hand against the spec, not by running an interpreter. seat-2's first answer differed at 3007, 3005 and 3008 because it let `deep` see the locals of `mid` and `outer`. The spec's scoping is per call, so `deep` reads the globals `a` = 1000 and `b` = 2000. seat-2 agreed and re-checked the rest, and seat-1's independent trace matched mine.

I've left the room.
